incidents.name: XBridge permissionless listToken then withdrawTokens
incidents.notes: XBridge.listToken() carried no access control, so the attacker listed the tokens already held by the bridge against a corresponding token of their choosing and then called withdrawTokens() to move the bridge's real deposits out.

sources.ref: onchain review: bridge proxy 0x47Ddb6A433B76117a98FBeAb5320D8b67D468e31 created 2023-10-20 by 0xfe6fb9ded2651fd325512657d34911d2fb5d646b, not the attacker; five EIP-1967 Upgraded events, the last at block 19720066 on 2024-04-23T19:05:23Z installing 0x354cca2f55dde182d36fe34d673430e226a3cb8c (the address the PoC header calls the vulnerable contract) — 12.2 hours before the exploit. The drain completes in a second transaction 0x903d88a92cbc0165a7f662305ac1bff97430dbcccaa0fe71e101e18aa9109c92; the deposit transaction recorded here is the one the PoC replays.
